title: Business Continuity, Incident Management & Internal Audit Manager
description: Innovate with purpose At BILL, we believe in empowering the businesses that drive our economy. By replacing outdated financial processes with innovative tools, we help businesses—from startups to established brands—make smarter decisions and gain control of their operations. And we don’t stop there: we’re creating the future of financial automation so businesses can spend more time on what matters. Working here means you become part of a vision-driven team that’s ready to tackle challenges and build cutting-edge solutions. We value purpose, drive, and curiosity—and we thrive in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment. We're remote-first, with office spaces in San Jose, CA and Draper, UT — and opportunities to connect in person when it counts. BILLders collaborate to deliver real impact for businesses that need more time in their busy weeks. BILL builds high performing teams and we seek to hire the best talent for every role. We're committed to building a workplace that fosters inclusion and diverse perspectives, valuing each person’s unique skills and experiences. We’d love to hear from you—you might be just what we’re looking for, whether in this role or another. ✨ Let’s give businesses more time for what matters. Make your impact at a leading Fintech Company BILL is seeking a Manager to lead the company's resilience program and contribute to the internal audit team. You will run the Business Continuity Management (BCM) program; own critical incident management and crisis response; and provide meaningful contributions to risk-based internal audit engagements.  What you will do Business continuity Lead the enterprise BCM program: policy, standards, playbooks, business impact analyses (BIAs), recovery strategies and annual plan reviews. Report program status, gaps and remediation progress to the LOB/functional BCM program leads and senior leadership. Plan and run tabletop exercises and recovery tests with LOBs, Cloud Infrastructure and InfoSec partners; use/develop internal AI tools to track findings to closure. Align BCM with Disaster Recovery and Crisis Management so recovery objectives and dependencies stay consistent. Incident management Own the critical incident management process: severity definitions, escalation paths, communications and on-call roles. Coordinate response during major disruptions and lead post-incident reviews with clear root causes, owners and due dates. Maintain incident metrics and trend reporting to show recurring risks and the status of corrective actions. Use/develop internal AI capabilities to create continuous monitoring and incident awareness notifications/communication.  Internal audit Execute the risk-based internal audit plan, including operational, financial, technology, compliance and third-party reviews. Plan and lead audits: scoping, risk and control matrices, TOD/TOE testing, produce workpapers, and clear, evidence-based reports. Use internal AI tools to execute testing and produce reporting as well as continuous monitoring when opportunities exist.  Track management action plans, validate remediation, and report open issues to leadership. Keep independence safeguards in place between audit work and the BCM and incident response functions you operate. Leadership Build credibility, trust and working relationships with our business partners.  What you bring 5 to 7 years in business continuity, incident or crisis management with at least 2 years leading BCM programs; 2+ years internal audit experience.  Hands-on experience with BCM, BIAs, recovery planning, incident response and audit methodology (risk assessment, audit planning, control testing, reporting) for FinTech, Payments and/or Software company(ies) is a non-negotiable. Familiarity with BCM, risk management and internal audit frameworks. Experience and/or strong desire to incorporate AI capabilities into your processes. Strong writing and presentation skills; able to brief executives clearly during pressure situations. Capable of providing credible challenge at all levels of the organization. Bachelor's degree in business, accounting, information systems or similar. Preferred: CIA, CISA, CRISC, CBCP/MBCP, CISSP or CPA. Visa Sponsorship:  Please note that this position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Applicants must have authorization to work in the United States without requiring visa sponsorship now or in the future. Our ranges for each role and job level are based on a variety of factors including candidate experience, expertise, and geographic location and may vary from the amounts listed below. The role is also eligible for a competitive benefits package that includes: medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, 401(k) retirement plan, flexible spending & health savings account, paid holidays, paid time off, and other company benefits. title: Director, Operations Accounting
description: CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at  www.coreweave.com . As the Director, Operations Accounting, you will serve as a strategic leader within CoreWeave’s Accounting Operations organization, with end-to-end ownership of the technical, operational, and reporting activities supporting our global data center operations. You will define and scale the accounting framework that supports rapid infrastructure growth, while ensuring financial integrity, strong internal controls, and alignment with business objectives. You will lead and develop a high-performing global team, partner closely with senior leadership across Operations, FP&A, and Technical Accounting, and play a key role in shaping the financial infrastructure that underpins CoreWeave’s expansion. This role reports to the Head of Operations Accounting and requires a balance of strategic vision, technical expertise, and operational execution — starting hands-on as a player-coach and scaling the team from there.   What You'll Do Own the function end to end: Provide strategic leadership over the technical, operational, and reporting activities supporting CoreWeave’s global data center operations — owning the accounting and month-end close for supply chain and inventory valuation, standard cost and absorption, fixed assets and capital project accounting (CIP), GRIR management, freight and logistics, and procure-to-pay (P2P). Establish the long-term vision: Define and drive a scalable operational accounting framework, including systems, workflows, and organizational design capable of sustaining hyper-growth. Build and operate the control environment: Design and execute a robust, SOX-compliant (or equivalent) control environment across operational and technical accounting processes, driving clean audits and year-over-year reductions in findings. Lead technical & judgment-heavy accounting: Evaluate, document, and implement accounting treatment for complex transactions in partnership with Technical Accounting and Controllership. Support the accounting review and ongoing management of long-term supplier and commercial agreements to ensure appropriate treatment and contractual alignment. Drive systems transformation & integrations: Own the accounting design for supply chain and fixed asset systems and integrations, including ERP implementations, migrations, or upgrades (e.g., NetSuite to Tier-1 platforms like SAP or Oracle), as well as sub-ledger and procurement/WMS integrations. Partner across the business: Act as a trusted advisor to Operations, Supply Chain, Procurement, FP&A, IT, Tax, Treasury, and Senior Leadership. Partner closely with FP&A on annual budgets, forecasts, and capital planning strategies to fix data at the source and ensure accurate, timely information flow. Lead audit readiness & operational excellence: Serve as the primary liaison with external auditors and Internal Audit to ensure timely, accurate deliverables. Continuously review existing processes to simplify, automate, shorten close timelines, and reduce operational risk. Build and scale a global team: Start as a hands-on player-coach, then hire, mentor, and grow a high-performing global team from a lean starting point. Who You Are (Required) 10+ years of progressive accounting experience , including senior leadership roles, with broad ownership of technical, operational, cost, or reporting accounting in a high-value, asset-heavy, capital-intensive, or logistics-intensive environment. Strong command of U.S. GAAP and internal controls: Deep technical background in U.S. GAAP as applied to inventory valuation, cost accounting, fixed assets/PP&E, CIP, and procure-to-pay, with proven experience designing and operating SOX-compliant (or equivalent) internal control frameworks. Systems & ERP transformation leadership: Hands-on experience leading or owning the accounting design for an ERP implementation, migration, or major upgrade (NetSuite, SAP, Oracle, Dynamics, or comparable). Proven team builder & player-coach: Demonstrated ability to lead, coach, and scale accounting teams in high-growth, fast-paced environments — equally comfortable setting long-term strategy and diving into technical execution. Exceptional leadership & stakeholder management: Strong executive presence and communication skills, with a track record of partnering cross-functionally with Operations, Supply Chain, Procurement, FP&A, and IT to achieve measurable outcomes.
